quote: my question around solar is gonna be not with that house
stewart_read: This is the pivotal disclosure of the call — the lead isn't for the address on file — and the rep doesn't probe what house, when, or why before continuing the standard pitch.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have been strategically continuing verify to get bill info first before addressing the future-home angle; but the rep never returns to clarify the future-home need at all, supporting the reactive miss read.
coaching_implication: Rep should have stopped and asked: 'tell me about the house you're planning to move to — timeline, location?' to requalify before continuing the current-address pitch.

stewart_read: Customer volunteers a specific product interest (solar shingles) — a genuine buying signal the rep could use to keep the conversation open even though Ion doesn't offer it yet.
coaching_implication: Rep correctly disclosed shingles are 1-2 years out, but didn't use the signal to pivot to what Ion does offer now (roofing, standard panels) as a bridge for the future home.

quote: I'm not planning on staying in that house for I'm probably looking to move probably in about three years
stewart_read: This is a timing/interest objection tied to the current house; instead of flipping it (e.g., anchoring on the bill they're paying now for three more years), rep pivots to a bill-amount question without addressing the objection.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have intentionally moved to bill-amount to build the bill-swap case before addressing timing — a legitimate sequencing choice — but he never circles back to counter the timing objection directly.
coaching_implication: Should flip: 'that's exactly why the bill swap makes sense — you'd rather pay a cheaper bill for those three years than the higher one, even before selling.'

quote: talked with my realtor, and he advised me not to do that if I'm looking to sell in the near future
stewart_read: A real estate authority objection (transferability concerns for a near-term sale) went unaddressed; rep pivoted to a no-cost installation reassurance instead of engaging the actual concern.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the realtor objection unwinnable and chosen to preserve rapport by not arguing — a defensible protocol read, but there was no attempt at even one counter-angle first.
coaching_implication: At minimum, rep should ask what specifically the realtor said about transfer, since bill-swap terms vary and misinformation is common; asking would have created an opening rather than conceding immediately.

quote: I wanna see what we could do for you because, like, your home is literally perfect for solar
stewart_read: Rep re-pitches savings and 'perfect for solar' claims on a house the customer already disqualified twice, rather than bridging to specialist or requalifying for the actual future home.
coaching_implication: Selling features and savings claims on a disqualified property wastes the call; the move should have been to requalify for the real target home or cleanly end the call.

quote: at this point in time, I'd probably say I probably don't wanna go any further then
stewart_read: Call ends with no next step, no offer to follow up when the customer is actually in the market for his next home, no capture of a future callback.
coaching_implication: Rep should have offered a future-dated touchpoint tied to the customer's ~3-year move timeline instead of just saying goodbye.
